title: Alignment of Glucose Conversion Factor, and Call for Cross-App Synchronization
body:
Diabetes management often requires the use of multiple interoperable apps (AAPS, xDrip, Nightscout, ...). To minimize confusion for users—especially those who are less experienced—it is vital that these apps operate consistently.

There is a conversion factor used to convert a glucose reading from mg/dL to mmol/L.  This is only needed if the user chooses to use mmol/L.  Otherwise, everything is always in mg/dL.
Historically, many systems used a factor of 18.0182. While this value still appears in some medical documentation, a more precise factor based on the actual molar mass of glucose is 18.01559.  

Nightscout (cgm-remote-monitor) changed their factor to reflect this more accurate value in 2025:
https://github.com/nightscout/cgm-remote-monitor/commit/0b731a06befae51955b004a30c83b9fdaf5ddbe1 

xDrip updated this factor in the last xDrip Nightly release (2026.06.24): https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/pull/4533 
As noted in that PR, even tiny discrepancies can lead to user confusion when data is shared across platforms.   

I have had difficulty locating a single, centralized conversion factor within the AAPS codebase. I suggest updating AAPS (wherever the conversion is defined) to use 18.01559 to ensure alignment with the rest of the ecosystem.  

A Call for Broader Cooperation:
Beyond this specific constant, this highlights a larger opportunity.  When core logic or "source of truth" constants change in one app, we currently lack a formal way to notify companion apps.   

I would like to invite the developers of AAPS, xDrip, and Nightscout to consider establishing a protocol for informing one another when making changes to shared logic like this.   Consistent math across our tools makes the entire ecosystem more robust and trustworthy for everyone.  

Thanks  

@psonnera @bewest
